narrative:
The model determined that you have a 58% probability of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeds the approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the loan amount you requested, the status of your checking account, and the status of your savings. The high amount you asked for—13,756 DM compared with an average of roughly 3,020 DM among approved applicants—was the single biggest reason the model leaned toward denial. It pushed the prediction noticeably toward bad credit risk because large loans carry higher risk for the bank.

Your checking-account status of “none” worked in your favor and was the second-most important factor. Most approved applicants (59%) also have no checking account, so this actually pulled the prediction somewhat toward approval. Similarly, having no savings or an unknown savings balance was the third-most influential detail. While this feature also nudged the outcome slightly toward good credit, its helpful effect was not strong enough to overcome the risk signaled by the very large loan size.

Taken together, the size of the requested loan outweighed the positive signals from your account and savings status, leading to the denial.

You should consider applying again with a substantially smaller loan amount, or take time to build a stronger savings record and positive checking-account activity before re-applying. These steps would directly address the main concerns the model raised. (218 words)
